immediateManagementPlan.intervention: STEP 1 - CARDIAC MEMBRANE STABILIZATION: IV Calcium Gluconate 10% 10–20 mL IV over 2–5 min (or Calcium Chloride 1g via central line)
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Immediately stabilize cardiac myocyte resting membrane potential against VF/asystole.

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: STEP 2 - INTRACELLULAR POTASSIUM SHIFTING: IV Regular Insulin 10 units + 50 mL D50W (25g Dextrose) + Inhaled Albuterol 10–20 mg nebulized
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Drive potassium into cells (lowers serum K+ by 0.5–1.2 mEq/L within 30 min).

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: STEP 3 - POTASSIUM ELIMINATION & EMERGENCE CONSULT: Emergent Nephrology Consultation for Hemodialysis and urinary catheterization

strictContraindications: Do NOT delay calcium administration when peaked T waves or QRS widening are present.
Do NOT administer potassium-sparing diuretics, ACEi/ARBs, or IV fluids containing potassium.
escalationTriggers: Widening QRS complex, sine-wave pattern, or refractory hyperkalemia -> Immediate Emergent Hemodialysis

guidelineCitations.guidelineName: Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury

title: Question 28 – Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
vignette: 36-year-old female presents with fever, confusion, petechiae, and fatigue. Hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL, platelets 18,000/µL, elevated LDH, and schistocytes on peripheral smear.

top5Differentials.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
top5Differentials.rationale: Classic pentad: Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia (schistocytes, high LDH, low Hb) + severe thrombocytopenia (18k) + neurological symptoms (confusion) + fever.

top5Differentials.name: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (Atypical HUS / Shiga-toxin HUS)
top5Differentials.rationale: MAHA and thrombocytopenia with dominant renal failure.

top5Differentials.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
top5Differentials.rationale: Consumptive coagulopathy; distinguished by abnormal PT/INR, aPTT, and low fibrinogen.

top5Differentials.name: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP) with Anemia
top5Differentials.rationale: Isolated thrombocytopenia; does NOT feature schistocytes or high LDH.

top5Differentials.name: Severe Sepsis / Meningococcemia with Purpura
top5Differentials.rationale: Fever, petechiae, and encephalopathy.

explicitMissingInformation: ADAMTS13 activity level and inhibitor titer (draw blood prior to plasma exchange)
Coagulation profile (PT/INR, aPTT, Fibrinogen: normal coags confirm TTP over DIC)
Serum Creatinine and pregnancy test

clinicalScores.clinicalMeaning: Platelets < 30k (+1), Hemolysis (+1), No cancer (+1), No transplant (+1), MCV < 90 (+1), INR < 1.5 (+1), Cr < 2.0 (+1). Strongly predicts severe ADAMTS13 deficiency; mandates immediate plasma exchange.

recommendedWorkup.action: Draw stat ADAMTS13 Activity and Inhibitor level PRIOR to plasma infusion (DO NOT WAIT FOR RESULTS)
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Definitive biomarker confirmation.

recommendedWorkup.action: Stat Peripheral Blood Smear (quantify schistocytes), Direct Coombs test, Haptoglobin, Reticulocyte count
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Confirm non-immune microangiopathic hemolytic anemia.

recommendedWorkup.action: Coagulation Panel (PT/INR, aPTT, Fibrinogen, D-dimer)
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Exclude DIC (coagulation profile is typically NORMAL in pure TTP).

contradictionsAndCaveats: PLATELET TRANSFUSIONS ARE STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN TTP: Transfusing platelets 'fuels the fire' by providing substrate for microvascular platelet thrombi, triggering fatal acute myocardial infarction and stroke! Platelets are indicated ONLY in catastrophic life-threatening hemorrhage!

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: EMERGENT THERAPEUTIC PLASMA EXCHANGE (PEX): 1.0–1.5 plasma volume exchange with Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) replacement
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Remove autoantibodies and replenish ADAMTS13 (reduces mortality from > 90% to < 15%).

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: High-Dose Corticosteroids: Methylprednisolone 1 g/day IV (or Prednisone 1 mg/kg/day)
Caplacizumab (anti-vWF nanobody) and Hematology Consultation

strictContraindications: Platelet transfusions are STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in TTP.
Do NOT wait for ADAMTS13 test results to initiate plasma exchange.
escalationTriggers: Fluctuating neurological deficits, seizures, or cardiac ischemia -> Emergent PEX initiation

guidelineCitations.issuingOrganization: International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH)
guidelineCitations.guidelineName: Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura

title: Question 29 – Opioid toxicity
vignette: 32-year-old male is found unconscious with RR 5/min, oxygen saturation 78%, pinpoint pupils, and minimal response to pain.

top5Differentials.name: Acute Opioid Overdose (Opioid Toxidrome)
top5Differentials.rationale: Classic opioid triad: Central nervous system depression (coma) + Severe respiratory depression (RR 5) + Miosis (pinpoint pupils).

top5Differentials.name: Pontine Hemorrhage
top5Differentials.rationale: Coma, pinpoint pupils, and abnormal breathing; non-responsive to naloxone.

top5Differentials.name: Sedative-Hypnotic Toxicity (Benzodiazepines, Barbiturates, GHB)
top5Differentials.rationale: CNS and respiratory depression; pupils typically normal or dilated.

top5Differentials.name: Severe Anoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
top5Differentials.rationale: Coma following prolonged unobserved hypoxemia.

top5Differentials.name: Severe Hypoglycemia
top5Differentials.rationale: Unresponsiveness and hypoventilation.

mustNotMissConditions: Co-ingestion with Acetaminophen or Fentanyl Analogs
explicitMissingInformation: Point-of-care blood glucose (immediate bedside test to rule out hypoglycemia)
Body temperature (hypothermia common in prolonged coma)
Arterial Blood Gas (degree of hypercapnic respiratory acidosis)

clinicalScores.clinicalMeaning: Miosis + Respiratory depression + Unconsciousness. Immediate indication for naloxone.

recommendedWorkup.action: Stat Point-of-Care Capillary Blood Glucose
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Rule out hypoglycemia mimic.

recommendedWorkup.action: Stat Acetaminophen level, Salicylate level, Blood Gas, CMP, Creatine Kinase (rhabdomyolysis)
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Rule out co-ingested toxins and compartment syndrome/rhabdomyolysis from prolonged immobilization.

contradictionsAndCaveats: BAG-VALVE-MASK VENTILATION MUST PRECEDE OR ACCOMPANY NALOXONE: Administering high-dose naloxone to a severely hypoxic patient (SpO2 78%) triggers massive sympathetic catecholamine surge, acute non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, and ventricular fibrillation! Oxygenate first!

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: AIRWAY AND VENTILATION FIRST: Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM) ventilatory support with 100% O2
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Reverse life-threatening hypoxia and hypercapnia prior to naloxone surge.

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: TITRATED NALOXONE: Naloxone 0.4 mg IV (or 2-4 mg IN) titrated to restore spontaneous respiratory rate >= 10-12/min, NOT full emergence
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Restore ventilation without triggering severe acute withdrawal or vomiting.

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: MANDATORY EXTENDED OBSERVATION: Monitor for at least 4–6 hours (or >= 24h for long-acting opioids like Methadone)
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Naloxone half-life (30-90 min) is much shorter than most opioids; monitor for renarcotization.

strictContraindications: Do NOT administer massive boluses of naloxone (e.g. 10 mg) in opioid-dependent patients without cardiac arrest (causes violent withdrawal, vomiting, aspiration, and flash pulmonary edema).
Do NOT discharge patient early after naloxone reversal.
escalationTriggers: Renarcotization (respiratory rate drops < 8/min) -> Start continuous IV Naloxone infusion (2/3 of waking dose per hour)

guidelineCitations.guidelineName: Focused Update on Adult Basic and Advanced Life Support: Opioid Overdose

title: Question 30 – Multiple drug overdose
vignette: 25-year-old female presents after an intentional ingestion of an unknown quantity of medication. She is drowsy, HR 118 bpm, BP 96/60 mmHg, and QTc 520 ms.

top5Differentials.name: Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA) / Sodium Channel Blocker Toxicity
top5Differentials.rationale: Tachycardia, hypotension, drowsiness, and cardiac conduction delay; high risk of seizures and refractory arrhythmias.

top5Differentials.name: QT-Prolonging Antipsychotic / Antidepressant Overdose (Quetiapine, Citalopram)
top5Differentials.rationale: Marked QTc prolongation (520 ms) with hypotension and lethargy; triggers Torsades de Pointes.

top5Differentials.name: Acetaminophen Co-Ingestion (Silent Lethal Ingestion)
top5Differentials.rationale: Frequently co-ingested in intentional overdoses; initially asymptomatic but causes fatal acute liver failure.

top5Differentials.name: Antihistamine / Anticholinergic Toxicity
top5Differentials.rationale: Tachycardia, drowsiness/delirium, and QTc widening.

top5Differentials.name: Serotonin Syndrome (SSRI/SNRI Overdose)
top5Differentials.rationale: Tachycardia, autonomic instability, and altered mental status.

mustNotMissConditions: TCA Sodium Channel Blocker Seizures & Shock
explicitMissingInformation: Stat 12-lead ECG QRS duration and terminal R-wave amplitude in lead aVR
Serum Acetaminophen and Salicylate levels (MANDATORY in all intentional overdoses)
Serum Potassium, Magnesium, and Calcium

clinicalScores.scoreName: Tisdale Risk Score for QT Prolongation
clinicalScores.clinicalMeaning: QTc 520 ms confers extreme risk for Torsades de Pointes and ventricular fibrillation.

recommendedWorkup.action: Stat 12-lead ECG with continuous telemetry and automated QRS/QTc monitoring
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Evaluate QRS widening (> 100 ms) and terminal R in aVR (> 3 mm).

recommendedWorkup.action: Stat 4-hour Serum Acetaminophen level, Salicylate level, Blood Glucose, Ethanol, BMP
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Detect occult lethal co-ingestions requiring N-acetylcysteine.

recommendedWorkup.action: Urine Pregnancy Test (beta-hCG) in all reproductive-age females
recommendedWorkup.rationale: Teratogen and obstetric management.

contradictionsAndCaveats: Class IA and IC antiarrhythmics (Procainamide, Flecainide) and QT-prolonging agents (Amiodarone) are ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED in drug-induced QTc prolongation or TCA toxicity: they worsen sodium channel blockade and trigger fatal arrhythmias!

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: IMMEDIATE POISON CONTROL CENTER CONSULTATION (1-800-222-1222) and continuous cardiac monitoring
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Expert toxicology management and antidotal guidance.

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: IV SODIUM BICARBONATE GATING: If QRS > 100 ms, ventricular arrhythmia, or severe hypotension occurs, administer IV Sodium Bicarbonate 1–2 mEq/kg boluses
immediateManagementPlan.objective: Outcompete sodium channel blockade and alkalinize serum (target pH 7.50–7.55).

immediateManagementPlan.intervention: TORSADES DE POINTES PROPHYLAXIS: IV Magnesium Sulfate 2g IV push if QTc > 500 ms with ventricular ectopy
N-ACETYLCYSTEINE (NAC) GATING: Initiate IV N-acetylcysteine immediately if 4-hour acetaminophen level crosses treatment line on Rumack-Matthew nomogram

strictContraindications: Do NOT administer Physostigmine in suspected TCA toxicity (causes asystolic cardiac arrest).
Do NOT administer Flumazenil for suspected benzodiazepine co-overdose (precipitates intractable refractory status epilepticus).
escalationTriggers: QRS widening > 100 ms, Torsades de Pointes, or seizures -> Stat IV Sodium Bicarbonate and ICU transfer
